item.dc:creator: MikulasKarpeta
item.content:encoded:
This is an example page. It's different from a blog post because it will stay in one place and will show up in your site navigation (in most themes). Most people start with an About page that introduces them to potential site visitors. It might say something like this:

Hi there! I'm a bike messenger by day, aspiring actor by night, and this is my website. I live in Los Angeles, have a great dog named Jack, and I like piña coladas. (And gettin' caught in the rain.)

...or something like this:

The XYZ Doohickey Company was founded in 1971, and has been providing quality doohickeys to the public ever since. Located in Gotham City, XYZ employs over 2,000 people and does all kinds of awesome things for the Gotham community.

As a new WordPress user, you should go to your dashboard to delete this page and create new pages for your content. Have fun!

item.title: Privacy Policy
item.dc:creator: MikulasKarpeta
item.content:encoded:
Who we are

Suggested text: Our website address is: http://neonio3.mikulaskarpeta.net.

Comments

Suggested text: When visitors leave comments on the site we collect the data shown in the comments form, and also the visitor’s IP address and browser user agent string to help spam detection.

An anonymized string created from your email address (also called a hash) may be provided to the Gravatar service to see if you are using it. The Gravatar service privacy policy is available here: https://automattic.com/privacy/. After approval of your comment, your profile picture is visible to the public in the context of your comment.

Media

Suggested text: If you upload images to the website, you should avoid uploading images with embedded location data (EXIF GPS) included. Visitors to the website can download and extract any location data from images on the website.

Cookies

Suggested text: If you leave a comment on our site you may opt-in to saving your name, email address and website in cookies. These are for your convenience so that you do not have to fill in your details again when you leave another comment. These cookies will last for one year.

If you visit our login page, we will set a temporary cookie to determine if your browser accepts cookies. This cookie contains no personal data and is discarded when you close your browser.

When you log in, we will also set up several cookies to save your login information and your screen display choices. Login cookies last for two days, and screen options cookies last for a year. If you select "Remember Me", your login will persist for two weeks. If you log out of your account, the login cookies will be removed.

If you edit or publish an article, an additional cookie will be saved in your browser. This cookie includes no personal data and simply indicates the post ID of the article you just edited. It expires after 1 day.

Embedded content from other websites

Suggested text: Articles on this site may include embedded content (e.g. videos, images, articles, etc.). Embedded content from other websites behaves in the exact same way as if the visitor has visited the other website.

These websites may collect data about you, use cookies, embed additional third-party tracking, and monitor your interaction with that embedded content, including tracking your interaction with the embedded content if you have an account and are logged in to that website.

Who we share your data with

Suggested text: If you request a password reset, your IP address will be included in the reset email.

How long we retain your data

Suggested text: If you leave a comment, the comment and its metadata are retained indefinitely. This is so we can recognize and approve any follow-up comments automatically instead of holding them in a moderation queue.

For users that register on our website (if any), we also store the personal information they provide in their user profile. All users can see, edit, or delete their personal information at any time (except they cannot change their username). Website administrators can also see and edit that information.

What rights you have over your data

Suggested text: If you have an account on this site, or have left comments, you can request to receive an exported file of the personal data we hold about you, including any data you have provided to us. You can also request that we erase any personal data we hold about you. This does not include any data we are obliged to keep for administrative, legal, or security purposes.

Where your data is sent

Suggested text: Visitor comments may be checked through an automated spam detection service.

item.content:encoded:
DIRECTOR, FILMMAKER

LUCAS
VEIL

I am a director and filmmaker with an eye that most people spend their entire careers trying to develop. Over a decade of commercials, branded content, and short films — I don't just capture moments, I architect them. My work isn't background noise. It's the thing people remember.

THEPHILOSOPHY

"Filmmaking is not about capturing reality. It's about constructing a better one. Every frame I shoot carries an intention. Every cut serves the story. Nothing I make is accidental, and nothing is forgettable."

MY JOURNEY

2026

FEATURE DIRECTOR

Directing his first feature while sustaining an exclusive roster of global brand campaigns. Operating at the peak of the craft.

2025

LEAD DIRECTOR

Directed award-winning campaigns for luxury automotive and fashion brands across three continents. The kind of work that earns its own reputation.

2023

INDEPENDENT FILMMAKER

Launched his own production company at 32. Within a year — three international awards and a Cannes shortlist. The industry noticed.

TECHNICAL
ARSENAL

Cinematography

Composing frames that carry weight. Every shot is a deliberate decision. Every sequence tells a story within a story.

Direction & Editing

From concept to final cut, maintaining total creative control. The result always speaks for itself — loudly.

COMMON INQUIRIES

I work across commercials, branded content, and short films — from challenger brands looking for their first proper campaign to established names who want something more than predictable. If there's a story worth telling and a client who won't settle for ordinary, I'm interested.

Every project starts with a conversation about what you're actually trying to say — not just what you think you want. From there I move through concept, pre-production, shoot, and post, staying close at every stage. Great film is iterative, and I don't let go until it's exactly right.

Both. The budget has to make sense for the scope, but the ambition matters more than the company size. I've made work for global brands and for scrappy startups with more vision than resources. What I won't do is make something forgettable, regardless of the budget.

It depends on scope. A social content package can turn around in two to three weeks. A commercial or branded film typically runs six to eight weeks from concept to delivery. For longer-form work, the timeline is whatever it needs to be — I'd rather give you honesty than rush something that matters.

Mostly: an honest brief, a real audience in mind, and the confidence to let me do what I do. The best clients aren't the most prescriptive — they're the ones who trust the process. Tell me what you're trying to achieve and who you're trying to reach. We'll figure out the rest from there.

READY TO STAND

item.title: Audi – Pure Form
item.dc:creator: MikulasKarpeta
item.content:encoded:
Audi – Pure Form

ROLE

PRODUCTION

CLIENT

AUDI

YEAR

2023

REACH

18M+

This campaign for Audi focuses on form, precision, and silence. Filmed in a stark circular space with controlled light, the car is presented as a sculptural object rather than a commodity. Every angle, reflection, and contour is revealed with deliberate slowness, allowing the audience to see design as performance.

The creative approach was based on restraint. No dialogue, no urban chase, no background distraction—only the car itself under a dome of light. The visuals treat engineering as art, with sound design reduced to subtle echoes that reinforce the atmosphere of calm control.

Creative Goals

  • Present Audi as a brand defined by clarity, precision, and modernity
  • Highlight design as narrative: lines, surfaces, and details become the story
  • Strip away cliché advertising tropes and return to cinematic minimalism

Outcome

Released across global channels in 2024, the spot was praised for its clarity and bold refusal of spectacle. It positioned Audi not just as a car brand but as an icon of modern design.

item.title: Eventide
item.dc:creator: MikulasKarpeta
item.content:encoded:
Eventide

ROLE

SCREENPLAY

GENRE

SCI-FI

YEAR

2024

FESTIVALS

Berlinale
Toronto

The Eventide is a science fiction film about isolation and survival at the edge of space. A lone astronaut drifts aboard a silent vessel, waiting for a signal that may never arrive. Surrounded by machinery and darkness, he confronts both the vast unknown outside and the fragile limits of his own endurance.

The film builds its tension not through action but through atmosphere. Minimal dialogue, slow pacing, and claustrophobic framing convey the fragility of human presence in the infinite void. The sterile corridors of the spacecraft become a psychological landscape, reflecting the thin line between resilience and despair.

Themes

  • Human solitude against the immensity of the cosmos
  • Technology as both protector and prison
  • The ambiguity of hope in extreme isolation

Reception

Premiered at Sitges Film Festival in 2025, Eventide was praised for its stark imagery and meditative approach to science fiction. Critics highlighted its visual restraint, emotional depth, and ability to turn silence into a narrative force.

item.title: Room with Curtains
item.dc:creator: MikulasKarpeta
item.content:encoded:
Room with Curtains

ROLE

DIRECTOR

GENRE

DRAMA

YEAR

2021

FESTIVALS

Sarajevo,
Palm Springs

Room with Curtains is a short film about silence, waiting, and the unspoken. The entire story unfolds inside a small apartment where time seems suspended. A woman looks out of the window, caught between memory and anticipation, while the muted light and restrained framing turn every gesture into meaning.

The film embraces minimalism: long static shots, natural light, and a muted color palette. There is no score, only the sounds of the room and the city outside, which become part of the narrative. The absence of explicit dialogue emphasizes the tension between inner life and outward calm.

Themes

  • Intimacy and solitude
  • The weight of unexpressed emotion
  • The passage of time in confined spaces

Reception

Premiered at Clermont-Ferrand Short Film Festival in 2021, Room with Curtains was noted for its restrained style and emotional precision. Critics praised its ability to turn ordinary domestic space into a stage for psychological drama.

item.title: Midnight Echoes
item.dc:creator: MikulasKarpeta
item.content:encoded:
Midnight Echoes

ROLE

VISUAL CONCEPT

GENRE

EXPERIMENTADRAMA

YEAR

2022

FESTIVALS

ROTTERDAM
VIENNALE

Midnight Echoes is a feature-length film exploring the solitude and intimacy of urban nights. Told almost entirely from within a moving car, the story unfolds through fleeting encounters, overheard fragments, and the rhythm of the city itself. Rain on glass, distorted neon lights, and passing strangers create a tapestry of moods, part documentary and part dream.

The film deliberately avoids conventional narrative arcs. Instead it immerses viewers in a meditative journey where the car becomes both shelter and lens. The minimal setup with one location, shifting light, and layered soundscape challenges the way cinematic space can carry emotion.

Themes

  • Isolation and connection in the modern metropolis
  • The poetics of everyday movement
  • The blurred line between reality and perception

Reception

Premiered at selected art house festivals in 2022, Night Drive was praised for its immersive atmosphere and formal experimentation. Critics highlighted its ability to transform simple drives into existential reflections, giving voice to the silent conversations of a city at night.

item.title: Benz Class C
item.dc:creator: MikulasKarpeta
item.content:encoded:
Benz Class C

ROLE

DIRECTOR

CLIENT

M-BENZ

YEAR

2025

REACH

12M+

This commercial for Mercedes-Benz was designed as a cinematic meditation on freedom, precision, and control. The narrative is stripped down to its essentials: a single vehicle navigating a mountain pass. Shot from above, the camera follows every curve of the serpentine road, amplifying both the challenge of the terrain and the confidence of the car.

The creative direction emphasized a cold, atmospheric palette. Light fog and muted tones create an environment that feels timeless, almost suspended, while the car becomes the only source of clarity and movement. The visual rhythm mirrors the sensation of driving—moments of anticipation, sudden acceleration, and quiet release.

Rather than rely on spectacle, the piece is built on restraint. The absence of dialogue or superimposed slogans allows the imagery itself to carry the brand’s values: elegance, engineering, and trust. Every frame was composed with minimalism in mind, letting the landscape breathe and the vehicle define the narrative.

Creative Goals

  • Position Mercedes-Benz as a brand that transcends function and enters the realm of cinematic storytelling.
  • Highlight the symbiosis between driver, machine, and environment.
  • Evoke the idea that the journey itself—full of twists and uncertainty—is as important as the destination.

Outcome

The film was released across digital platforms and selected broadcast spots, praised for its stripped-down elegance and emotional weight. It proved that luxury can be expressed not through excess, but through clarity of vision.

item.title: Vertical City
item.dc:creator: MikulasKarpeta
item.content:encoded:
Vertical City

ROLE

DOP

GENRE

DOCUMENTARY

YEAR

2024

FESTIVALS

Sheffield,
DocFest, IDFA

Vertical City is a documentary film examining the rise of corporate architecture and its impact on urban life. Shot across several financial districts, the film uses stark geometry and reflective surfaces to explore how buildings shape not only skylines but also the psychology of those who move among them.

The visual language relies on long takes, upward angles, and shifting reflections. These perspectives emphasize scale and detachment, suggesting a modern landscape where glass and steel dominate the horizon while human presence feels diminished.

Focus

  • The symbolic power of architecture in global capitalism
  • The tension between monumental structures and everyday life
  • The transformation of public space into corporate territory

Reception

Premiered in 2024 at the Copenhagen Architecture Film Festival, Vertical City was described as “an unsettling meditation on the politics of design.” Its minimalist aesthetic and interview-driven narrative drew attention to the silent authority of high-rise buildings in shaping our collective imagination.

item.title: Russian Wheel
item.dc:creator: MikulasKarpeta
item.content:encoded:
Russian Wheel

ROLE

DIRECTOR

GENRE

COMMERCIAL

YEAR

2022

CLIENT

VOLANTE
OUTDOOR

Russian Wheel is a 60-second brand film for Volante Outdoor, a European adventure gear company launching its first global campaign. The brief asked for something that felt more like cinema than advertising — images of landscape and movement that let the product exist within a genuine context rather than a staged one.

Filmed across the Scottish Highlands and the coast of western Norway over 12 shoot days, the film follows a lone figure navigating extreme terrain at the edge of the seasons. No voiceover, no product close-ups. The brand appears only in behavior — the way a person moves when the equipment does exactly what it should.

Themes

  • Solitude as freedom, not isolation
  • Trust between body and environment
  • Restraint as a form of storytelling

Reception

Russian Wheel won a Cannes Lions Bronze in the Film Craft category and was shortlisted at D&AD. The campaign exceeded projected engagement benchmarks by 340% and has since been cited in industry press as a case study for narrative-led outdoor brand work.

item.title: After the Rain
item.dc:creator: MikulasKarpeta
item.content:encoded:
After the Rain

ROLE

DIRECTOR OF
PHOTOGRAPHY

GENRE

DOCUMENTARY

YEAR

2022

FESTIVALS

Tribeca,
DOC NYC

After the Rain is a feature documentary following three small-scale farmers across a single growing season in rural Portugal. Filmed over six months, the project required adapting to unpredictable weather, fragile trust, and the rhythms of agricultural life that resist any imposed schedule. The camera becomes a quiet witness rather than an observer.

The visual approach prioritizes available light and natural texture — early morning fog, the silver of irrigation pipes, soil that changes color as the season turns. A handheld intimacy was balanced against moments of wide, composed stillness to reflect both the labor and the contemplation that defines the farmers' daily existence.

Themes

  • Land, labor, and seasonal time
  • Human dependence on natural systems
  • Resilience in the face of climate uncertainty

Reception

Selected for the Tribeca Film Festival in 2022 and later screened at DOC NYC, After the Rain was recognized for its patient, luminous cinematography. Reviewers noted the rare quality of images that feel genuinely earned rather than composed — a portrait of work that honors the dignity of its subjects.

item.title: Neon Drift
item.dc:creator: MikulasKarpeta
item.content:encoded:
Neon Drift

ROLE

DIRECTOR

GENRE

MUSIC VIDEO

YEAR

2023

ARTIST

VALE LUNA

Neon Drift is a music video for electronic artist Vale Luna, shot over two nights across the highway interchanges and shuttered storefronts of a post-industrial city. The brief called for something visceral and kinetic — a visual counterpart to the track's layered tension between momentum and stillness.

The treatment draws from car chase films of the 1970s and contemporary night photography, using long exposures, in-camera flares, and a restricted palette of deep blue and amber. The performer moves through environments rather than performing within them, becoming part of the city's infrastructure rather than a figure set against it.

Themes

  • Urban anonymity and nocturnal energy
  • Speed as emotional state
  • The body lost in built environments

Reception

Released alongside the single in early 2023, Neon Drift accumulated over 2 million views within its first month and was featured in Pitchfork's roundup of the year's best music videos. Directors Notes cited the night cinematography as some of the most technically assured work in the genre that year.

item.title: The Last Letter
item.dc:creator: MikulasKarpeta
item.content:encoded:
The Last Letter

ROLE

DIRECTOR &
WRITER

GENRE

THRILLER

YEAR

2020

FESTIVALS

Sundance,
Edinburgh

The Last Letter is a short thriller set over the course of one sleepless night. A man discovers a handwritten letter addressed to someone who no longer exists — and begins retracing a relationship he thought he understood. The film is constructed around misdirection and the slow collapse of certainty.

Shot on 16mm to preserve grain and unpredictability, the visual language deliberately avoids clean resolution — shallow focus, obscured sightlines, and tight framing that keeps the audience slightly off-balance throughout. The edit mirrors the protagonist's mental state: deceptively calm on the surface, increasingly fractured underneath.

Themes

  • Unreliable memory and self-deception
  • Guilt and the revisitation of the past
  • Language as concealment

Reception

World premiere at Sundance 2020 in the Midnight Shorts program, followed by a selection at Edinburgh International Film Festival. The Last Letter was described by Variety as "a tightly wound debut that earns every twist" — a rare compliment for a film so committed to withholding.

item.title: Undertow
item.dc:creator: MikulasKarpeta
item.content:encoded:
Undertow

ROLE

EDITOR

GENRE

FEATURE FILM

YEAR

2023

FESTIVALS

Toronto,
Rotterdam

Undertow is a 94-minute feature that follows two estranged brothers reunited by a family emergency in a coastal fishing town. Directed by Ana Ferreira, the film was assembled from over 300 hours of footage shot across four seasons, requiring an editorial approach that could hold both the sprawl of real time and the compression of dramatic necessity.

The editing builds rhythm from silence as much as from action — long takes interrupted by sudden cuts, conversations that begin in one location and resolve in another. The goal was to let the landscape into the film's emotional structure: the sea's indifference as an ironic counterpoint to the brothers' intensity, not merely backdrop.

Themes

  • Fraternal loyalty and its limits
  • Inheritance — of place, of trauma, of silence
  • The impossibility of return

Reception

World premiere at the Toronto International Film Festival 2023, followed by the International Film Festival Rotterdam. Undertow received particular critical attention for its editing, with The Hollywood Reporter calling it "a masterclass in restraint — knowing exactly when to stay and when to cut away."

item.title: Glass Hours
item.dc:creator: MikulasKarpeta
item.content:encoded:
Glass Hours

ROLE

DIRECTOR

GENRE

EXPERIMENTAL

YEAR

2024

SCREENINGS

SXSW,
Viennale

Glass Hours is a 22-minute experimental film composed entirely from footage shot inside glass structures — a greenhouse, an office atrium, an empty aquarium, a hospital corridor. The project began as a study of refraction and became something closer to an essay on visibility: what it means to be seen through a surface, and what the surface withholds.

There is no narrative in the conventional sense. Instead, the film moves associatively — connections between spaces are established through light behavior, repeated gesture, and a spatial score composed specifically for the film by a collaborating sound artist. Each environment was shot at a different hour of the day to track how glass holds and transforms natural light across time.

Themes

  • Transparency and its illusions
  • The architecture of surveillance and care
  • Light as both medium and subject

Reception

Premiered in the Experimental Shorts program at SXSW 2024 and subsequently screened at the Viennale. Glass Hours was acquired by the International Short Film Archive and described by Sight & Sound as "a rigorously conceived meditation on transparency — visually immaculate and quietly unsettling."
